Rashi on Shevuot 5a:10:1.hebrew: אין האיש מנוקה מעון - שבא עליה אחר שנסתרה:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:10:1.english: The husband is not free of sin - [Meaning,] that he had relations with her after she secluded herself [with the other man].

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:12:1.hebrew: ידיעת בית רבו - שלמד בבית רבו שהנוגע בטומאה טמא, והוא ידע שהרגיש כשנגע, אבל לא התבונן לשום על לבו שנטמא (בטומאה כשנוגע בה) — שמה ידיעה:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:12:1.english: Knowledge [acquired in] the house of his teacher - That he learned in the house of his teacher that one who touches impurity is impure, and he knew that he felt [it] when he touched, but he did not reflect to take to heart that he had become impure (through impurity, when he touches it) — this is called "knowledge."

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:14:1.hebrew: ד' בפנים - שתים לחיוב, הכנסה דעני והכנסה דבעל הבית, וב' לפטור, כשזה עוקר וזה מניח, דכתיב "בעשותה" — העושה את כולה (שבת דף ג.):
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:14:1.english: Four inside - Two [cases] of liability: the bringing in of the poor person [i.e., the poor person's hand reaching into the house] and the bringing in of the householder; and two [cases] of exemption, when this one lifts and that one places [the object], as it is written, "in his doing it" (Leviticus 4:27) — [meaning] one who does the whole of it (Shabbat 3a).

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:15:1.hebrew: דעיקר שבת - שעיקר מסכת באיסורי שבת:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:15:1.english: For the main [discussion] of Shabbat - For the main [subject] of the tractate is the prohibitions of Shabbat.

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:15:2.hebrew: אבות - יציאות השבת שהן מן התורה:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:15:2.english: Primary categories - The [forms of] carrying out [on Shabbat] that are from the Torah.

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:15:3.english: Subcategories - The [acts of] bringing in, which are not explicitly specified.

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:16:1.hebrew: תרתי הויין - ומתני' דהכא ד' תנן:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:16:1.english: They are two - But the mishna here, we learned [that there are] four.

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:17:1.hebrew: שתים לחיוב - הוצאה דעני, והוצאה דבעל הבית:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:17:1.english: Two for liability - The carrying out of the poor person, and the carrying out of the homeowner.

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:17:2.hebrew: ושתים לפטור - אחת, שהעני פושט ידו לפנים, ונתן בעה"ב לתוכה, והעני הוציאה ועבד. איהו הנחה ולא עבד עקיר', ובעה"ב עקר ולא הניח, ושניהם פטורין. ואחת, שבעה"ב פושט ידו מליאה לחוץ, ונטל העני מתוכה והניח, דעבד נמי בעל הבית עקירה והעני הנחה, ושניהם פטורין בשתי הוצאות הללו:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:17:2.english: And two for exemption - One [is where] the poor person extends his hand inside, and the householder places [an object] into it, and the poor person carries it out and acts [i.e., completes the act]. He performed the placing down but did not perform the lifting, and the householder performed the lifting but did not place it down, and both are exempt. And [the other is where] the householder extends his hand, full, outside, and the poor person takes from it and places [the object] down, so that the householder too performed the lifting and the poor person the placing down, and both are exempt in these two [cases of] carrying out.

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:19:1.hebrew: חיובי מאי נינהו יציאות - דהא יציאות קתני, ויציאות דחיובא תרתי הוא דהויין: חדא דעני, וחדא דבעה"ב:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:19:1.english: What are the cases of liability? Carrying out - For [the Mishnah] teaches "carrying out," yet the acts of carrying out that involve liability are only two: one of the poor person, and one of the homeowner.

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:1:1.hebrew: ריבויי ומיעוטי - וריבה הכל, ומיעט. סם הכי מפרש לה בקדושין:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:1:1.english: Amplifications and restrictions - [The verse] amplified everything, and [then] restricted. Thus it is explained in [tractate] Kiddushin.

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:2:1.hebrew: והכא - גבי פדיון הבן, להכי דריש ליה בריבויי ומיעוטי, משום דאין הפרט בין שני כללות:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:2:1.english: And here - with regard to the redemption of the firstborn, the reason he expounds it by way of amplifications and restrictions is because a detail [that appears] between two generalizations [is not treated as a detail in the manner of the generalizations-and-details method]:

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:2:2.hebrew: כדתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל - באלו טריפות, דאיכא תנא דדריש את זה תאכלו מכל אשר במים: כלל, בימים ובנחלים: פרט, במים: חזר וכלל. ופליג עליה תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל ואמר: במים במים סמוכין זה לזה, ואח"כ כתיב בימים ובנחלים. הלכך אין זה כלל ופרט, אלא הטילהו ביניהם לדרשו בריבויי ומיעוטי:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:2:2.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught - Regarding these [laws of] tereifot, for there is a Tanna who expounds: "These you may eat, of all that are in the waters" — a generalization; "in the seas and in the rivers" — a detail; "in the waters" — again a generalization. And the school of Rabbi Yishmael disagrees with him and says: "In the waters" and "in the waters" are adjacent to one another, and afterward "in the seas and in the rivers" is written. Therefore this is not a generalization and a detail; rather, [the Torah] placed them [the seas and rivers] between them in order to expound it by the method of amplifications and restrictions:

Rashi on Shevuot 5a:4:1.hebrew: ורבנן - דפליגי עליה דרבי, ודרשי ליה בכלל ופרט, סבירא להו הדרשה כדאמרי במערבא:
Rashi on Shevuot 5a:4:1.english: And the Rabbis - who disagree with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] and expound it [the verse] as a generalization and a detail, hold [this derivation] in accordance with what they say in the West [Eretz Yisrael]:

Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:12:1.hebrew: ידיעת בית רבו שמה ידיעה - אף על פי שדבר זה לא נעלם ממנו, שגם עתה יודע כן, ולא אתי למעוטי אלא תינוק שנשבה. וכן בסוטה: יודע שאם נטמאה אסורה. וגבי תורה נמי, אף בשעת העלמה נמי יודע שהיא בעולם:
Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:12:1.english: The knowledge [acquired in] his teacher's house is called knowledge - Even though this matter was not hidden from him, [as] even now he knows it so, and [the verse] comes to exclude only a child who was taken captive. And so too with a *sotah*: he knows that if she became impure she is forbidden [to him]. And with regard to Torah as well, even at the time of the lapse [of awareness] he nevertheless knows that it exists in the world:

Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:14:1.hebrew: שתים שהן ד' בפנים - הכא פי' בקונטרס: בפנים היינו הכנסות, ובחוץ היינו הוצאות. ואין נראה, מדאיצטריך לקמן למימר וקמפרש הכנסה לאלתר, ה"ל לאוכוחי משתים שהן ד' בפנים דהוו כולהו הכנסה. ונראה כמו שפירש בקונטרס במסכת שבת (דף ב.): שתים הוצאה והכנסה דחיוב של בעל הבית העומד בפנים, שהן ארבע הוצאה והכנסה דפטור; ובחוץ לעני העומד בחוץ. וריב"א פירש: שתים דהוצאה דחיוב והוצאה דפטור, שהן ד' הכנסה דחיוב ודפטור לבעל הבית העומד בפנים, וכן לעני העומד בחוץ. דה"נ מפרש לעיל מתני' דהכא: שתים הוצאה דעני ודבעל הבית, שהן ד' הכנסה דעני ודבעל הבית. ובירושלמי בעיא אי איכא לפרושי מתני' כמו שפירש בקונט' או כריב"א, ואין להאריך. ואין להקשות לפירוש ריב"א, הא דמפרש ואזיל במתני' דשבת כסדר הקונט' הכנסה והוצאה דעני, ולא מפרש הוצאה והוצאה, הכנסה והכנסה — דניחא ליה למינקט הכי כדי לקצר: פשט עני ידו לפנים, או שנטל כו', והוצאה והוצאה היה צריך להאריך. ועוי"ל, שתים שהן ד' בפנים היינו חיוב שחייב ומביא קרבן עליהם בפנים בעזרה, דהיינו ב' הוצאות וב' הכנסות; ושתים שהן ד' בחוץ היינו פטור:
Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:14:1.english: Two that are four, inside - Here, Rashi explained: "inside" means bringing in, and "outside" means taking out. But this does not seem [correct], since later it needed to say and explain "bringing in" immediately; it should have proven this from "two that are four inside," which would all be bringing in. Rather, it appears [that the mishna in Shabbat should be understood] as Rashi explained in tractate Shabbat (2a): Two [acts] — taking out and bringing in — for which the householder standing inside is liable, which are four [when counting] taking out and bringing in for which he is exempt; and [likewise] outside, for the poor person standing outside. Rabbeinu Yitzchak ben Asher (Ri"v) explained: Two — taking out that is liable and taking out that is exempt — which are four [when counting] bringing in that is liable and exempt, for the householder standing inside and likewise for the poor person standing outside. For so too does [the Gemara] explain above the mishna here: Two [types of] taking out, that of the poor person and that of the householder, which are four [when counting] the bringing in of the poor person and of the householder. And in the Yerushalmi the question is raised whether the mishna can be explained as Rashi explained, or as the Ri"v [explained], and there is no need to elaborate. One should not object to the Ri"v's explanation from the fact that [the Gemara] explains, proceeding through the mishna in Shabbat in order, only bringing in and taking out of the poor person, and does not explain taking out and taking out, bringing in and bringing in — because it was convenient for it to state it this way in order to be brief: "The poor person stretched his hand inside, or he took, etc."; whereas [for] taking out and taking out it would have had to be lengthy. And furthermore, [one can explain that] "two that are four, inside" refers to liability, where one is liable and brings a sacrifice for them inside, in the Temple courtyard, namely two [types of] taking out and two [types of] bringing in; and "two that are four, outside" refers to exemption:

Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:14:2.hebrew: ומאי שנא הכא דתני שתים שהן ד' ותו לא - וא"ת: ולישני דהכא לא מצי תני כי התם, משום דדומיא דמראות נגעים קתני כולהו לחיובא? וי"ל: דשפיר הוה דומיא דמראות נגעים, הואיל ואיכא בהו ד' לחיובא. והר"ר משה פירש: משום דומיא דמראות נגעים אין לו להניח מלפרש דיני שבת, אבל בתר דמסיק דהכא לאו עיקר שבת הוא, פריך שפיר: והא דומיא דמראות נגעים קתני:
Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:14:2.english: "And what is different here, that it teaches 'two that are four' and no more" - And if you ask: But let [the Gemara] answer that here [the Mishnah] cannot teach as it does there, because it teaches them all as cases of liability, similar to the [Mishnah's list of] appearances of leprosy-signs? And one can answer: It would indeed be similar to the appearances of leprosy-signs, since there are four [cases] among them of liability. And Rabbi Moshe explained: Because [the Mishnah here teaches] similarly to the appearances of leprosy-signs, [the Tanna] has no reason to refrain from explaining the laws of Shabbat. But after [the Gemara] concludes that here [the Mishnah] is not the main [discussion] of Shabbat, it asks well: But it teaches [this] similarly to the appearances of leprosy-signs!

Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:15:1.hebrew: אבות תני תולדות לא תני - אע"ג דבמראות נגעים תני אבות ותולדות, התם משום דאי אפשר למצוא ב' שהן ד' בענין אחר:
Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:15:1.english: It teaches primary categories; it does not teach subcategories - Even though in [the mishnah on] the appearances of leprous marks (Nega'im) it teaches both primary categories and subcategories, there [it is] because it is impossible to find two [primary categories] that are four in another manner:

Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:20:1.hebrew: והא יציאות קתני - לפי הפשט משמע דלא פריך אלא אהך דהכא, משום דלא תני פטורי. אבל אההיא דשבת דתני חיובי ופטורי — ניחא ליה. ותימה, דהיכי משכחת לה בהוצאות גרידא ב' שהן ד' לבעל הבית, וכן לעני? ומפרש ר"י דהשתא חשיב אף פטור דפטור ומותר, דמשכחת כל הח' בהוצאות:
Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:20:1.english: "But it teaches 'acts of carrying out'" - According to the simple reading, it seems that [the Gemara] objects only to this [mishna] here, because it does not teach the exempt cases. But regarding that [mishna] in Shabbat, which teaches both the liable and the exempt cases, [the Gemara] is satisfied. And this is puzzling: how can [all the cases] be found with acts of carrying out alone — two that are four for the homeowner, and likewise for the poor person? And Rabbi Yitzchak explains that now [the Mishnah] counts even [the case of] exempt-and-permitted as an exemption, so that all eight are found in acts of carrying out:

Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:3:1.hebrew: דתנא דבי ר' ישמעאל במים במים שני פעמים כו' - תימה: דר' ישמעאל תני בי"ג מדות התורה נדרשת, והא איכא טפי הך מדה, דשני כללות הסמוכו' דדרשינן בריבה ומיעט:
Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:3:1.english: "As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: 'In the water, in the water,' twice," etc. - This is puzzling: Rabbi Yishmael taught that the Torah is expounded by thirteen principles, yet there is an additional principle here — that of two adjacent generalizations, which we expound as an amplification and a restriction:

Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:5:1.hebrew: בשבועות נסיב לה כר' עקיבא ולא סבר לה - זימנין דלא בעי למימר הכי. בפרק כיסוי הדם (חולין דף פה:) גבי רבי חייא דנפל ליה יניכה בכיתני', וא"ל רבי: צא ונחור. ופריך: ולימא ליה צא וטרוף! דהא רבי ראה דבריו של ר"ש בכיסוי הדם, ושנאם בלשון חכמים, דשחיטה שאינה ראויה לא שמה שחיטה. ולא בעי למימר תני לה ולא סבר לה:
Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:5:1.english: "With regard to oaths, he formulated it like Rabbi Akiva, but he does not hold accordingly" - Sometimes he did not want to say this. In the chapter Kisui HaDam (Chullin 85b), concerning Rabbi Chiya, to whom a yenikha happened in his kitani, Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] said to him: "Go out and naḥor." And [the Gemara] asks: But let him say to him, "Go out and tear it [as a tereifah]!" For Rabbi saw the words of Rabbi Shimon in [the chapter] Kisui HaDam, and he taught them in the language of the Sages, [holding] that a slaughter that is not fit is not called slaughter. And [the Gemara there] did not want to say: He taught it but does not hold accordingly:

Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:7:1.hebrew: ונעלם מעיני אישה מכלל דה"ל ידיעה מעיקרא - י"מ דה"ל ידיעה שנטמאת, דהכי משמע קרא: "ושכב איש אותה שכבת זרע ונעלם" וגו'. וקשה לפירוש זה, דהיכי דמי? אי בשעת השקאה נזכר מן הטומאה, למה משקה אותה? ואם אינו נזכר, אמאי משקה אותה? הא בעינן ידיעה מעיקרא, והוא סבור שלא היתה לו ידיעה מעולם. ומיהו יש ליישב דמיירי כשאינו נזכר, ומ"מ משקה אותה מספק, דע"י השקאה יתברר אם היתה לו ידיעה מעיקרא או לאו. ולפי המפרשים דונעלם קאי אסתירה, מיירי שפיר, דבשעת השקאה זכור מן הסתירה. אבל מ"מ קשה: אמאי חשיב ליה "אין מנוקה" אם לא בא עליה משנסתרה? וי"ל: כיון דשכח, מוכיח שלא הקפיד, ולא חשיב מנוקה מעון, דאפילו אינו מוחה אעון בניו ובנותיו, אין מים בודקין את אשתו, כדאיתא בפ"ב דסוטה (דף מז:). ואמר נמי התם: אם אתם מקפידין על עצמכם, המים בודקין את נשותיכם:
Tosafot on Shevuot 5a:7:1.english: "And it was concealed from the eyes of her husband" — by implication, he had knowledge initially - Some explain: he had knowledge that she became impure, for this is how the verse implies: "And a man lies with her carnally, and it is concealed..." etc. But this explanation is difficult: what is the case? If at the time of the drinking he remembers the impurity, why does he give her to drink? And if he does not remember, why does he give her to drink? Surely we require knowledge at the outset, and he thinks that he never had such knowledge! However, it can be resolved that [the Gemara] is speaking of where he does not remember, and nevertheless he gives her to drink out of uncertainty, since through the drinking it will become clear whether he had knowledge initially or not. And according to the commentators who say that "and it was concealed" refers to the seclusion, it is well explained, since at the time of the drinking he remembers the seclusion. But nevertheless it is difficult: why does [the verse] consider him "not clean" if he did not have relations with her after she secluded herself? And one can say: since he forgot, this proves that he was not scrupulous, and he is not considered clean of sin. For even if he does not protest the sin of his sons and daughters, the water does not test his wife, as is stated in the second chapter of Sotah (47b). And it also says there: If you are scrupulous about yourselves, the water will test your wives.
